cards.text: This one's a song of ascents, and the psalm calls on Israel to declare it. Israel says, "Many a time they have persecuted me from my youth…" Not once. Many a time.
Then Israel says it again: many a time, from youth. But this time the line keeps going.

cards.question: Israel has been persecuted many a time, from youth. What does Israel say about the persecutors?

answers.text: They have not prevailed against Israel
They drove Israel far from home

cards.text: Then Israel paints a picture: "The plowmen plowed over my back…" I think this one hurts.

cards.question: Israel has been persecuted many a time, from youth. In the plowing picture, Israel says the plowmen made their furrows short.

cards.text: But right here, the song turns. Israel stops talking about the plowmen and starts talking about the LORD.

cards.question: After all those years of persecution, Israel calls the LORD righteous.
After the picture of the plowmen, Israel turns to the LORD. What does Israel say the LORD has done?

answers.text: Cut Israel from the cords of the wicked
Taught Israel to plow its own fields
Told Israel to wait a little longer

cards.question: Then the psalm turns to all who hate Zion, the city of Jerusalem. What does it wish for them?

answers.text: That they be turned back in shame
That they be welcomed into Zion
That they be made rulers of Zion

cards.text: Then the psalm gives a picture for the ones who hate Zion. May they be like grass on the rooftops.

cards.question: The psalm wishes the ones who hate Zion would be like grass on the rooftops, which ___ before it can grow.

cards.text: Nothing to fill the reaper's hands, nothing for the arms of the binder of sheaves. That's dough I left out so long it dried up before it ever SAW the oven, and nobody's filling a cookie box with THAT.

cards.question: Last line. The psalm has wished shame and withering on the ones who hate Zion. What does it wish no one passing by would say to them?

answers.text: The blessing of the LORD be on you
The LORD sees what you have done
You will never take Zion from us

cards.text: The line keeps going with "…we bless you in the name of the LORD." The psalm wishes no one walking by would say that either, and that's where the song ends.
